audit.why: Both layers agree on Akshan 7/7 and the FAVOURED 4/10 read is consistent with a champion who cannot kill Akshan at contact and whose only answers displace rather than stop. The 50.11% win rate over 924 games sits below what an 8/10 chart implies, so I have left the sides alone but grounded the why-texts in his actual cooldowns rather than raising or lowering ratings without evidence.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes were written as though Ziggs simply loses at range and dies to any dive, with the level 6 spike claiming his ultimate is irrelevant and the first-item spike claiming a one-shot.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb is 850 range — identical to Avengerang — and recharges every 6 down to 4 seconds against Akshan's 9 down to 5. Mega Inferno Bomb is 5000 range and 120 seconds: it never enters the duel, but it does take waves and punish recalls. Satchel Charge is the reason a dive fails, and it is 20 seconds at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Spikes keyed to Satchel Charge (20s) and Hexplosive Minefield (16s flat) being spent, not to range superiority Akshan does not have.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told the player to land 'empowered autos' in 'melee-auto range' — Akshan is ranged and has no empowered auto — and never mentioned that Satchel Charge displaces, or that Hexplosive Minefield exists as the anti-approach tool.
audit.why: Satchel Charge knocks enemies away (and Ziggs himself), so it does not just create distance — it can move him out of a Comeuppance release, which is a first-champion-hit projectile. The minefield slows on contact every 16 seconds and is what actually taxes a swing-in.
audit.corrected: Swing in on a spent Satchel or minefield; hold the ultimate release for after Satchel fires rather than into it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json W text 'knocking them away', E text

audit.why: Ziggs' Q, your Q, your autos and your R bullets are all projectiles, but neither champion has a projectile-blocking tool, so nothing actionable follows.

edits.after: Akshan wins early trades: same 850 range on the boomerang, but his three-hit string carries a shield and Ziggs has none.

edits.before: Heading into six the same all-in pattern keeps working, cementing Akshan's lane lead.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb is up every 4.5s against your 6s Q — trade at contact, not at range.

edits.before: Akshan's first-item passive burst one-shots Ziggs in an all-in, making this the biggest spike of the matchup.
edits.after: Your first item plus the swing's autos kills him inside one Satchel Charge cooldown — the matchup's biggest spike.

edits.after: Late he is a pick for your R: no dash, no escape but Satchel Charge, and 5000-range poke that gives his position away.

edits.before: Ziggs' satchel-and-bomb spam pokes your wave but you can close distance with E and punish his squishy frame hard once you're in melee-auto range.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb matches your 850 range and comes back every 5 seconds, so range is not the fight — Heroic Swing onto him is, and Satchel is 20s.

edits.before: Mega Inferno Bomb threatens your recalls and wave state, but it doesn't change the fact you can dive him down before he ever gets to use it in a duel.
edits.after: Mega Inferno Bomb is 5000 range and 120 seconds at rank 1 — it takes your waves and punishes recalls, but in a duel it is not a spell he gets to cast.

edits.before: Your passive stacking one-shots Ziggs in a single all-in once your first item lands — he simply can't out-trade you at close range.
edits.after: Once your first item lands, one three-hit string plus swing autos is his whole health bar — but open with Satchel spent, or it throws you off.

edits.before: You use Heroic Swing to close the gap before Ziggs can kite with his bombs, and Comeuppance guarantees the pick if he tries to disengage.
edits.after: Heroic Swing closes the gap before he can kite, and Comeuppance finishes the disengage — but Satchel moves him too, so fire after it, not into it.

edits.before: Ziggs wants to sit at max range and chip you with Q and bomb-and-mine setups, but he has almost no escape once you're inside his kit's short leash. Use E to jump the wall or gap and land empowered autos before he can satchel away. As long as you don't walk face-first into his bomb combo on cooldown, your all-in wins nearly every close-range exchange.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb is 850 range, the same as your boomerang, and it recharges faster than yours — so do not settle for a poke war. His stopping power is Hexplosive Minefield on 16 seconds and Satchel Charge on 20, both of which push you back rather than kill you. Swing in once one of them is spent and the three-hit string does the rest.

edits.before: Ziggs' ult threatens your tower and recall timing around Lvl 6, but it changes nothing about the 1v1 — he still melts if you get on top of him. Watch for satchel charges up before committing your all-in, since that's his only real disengage tool. Keep applying pressure with short trades and dives whenever his cooldowns are down; he has no way to out-scale you in lane.
edits.after: Mega Inferno Bomb reaches 5000 range on a 120-second cooldown, so it takes waves and punishes recalls without ever entering the duel. Satchel Charge is his only disengage — it knocks him away as well as you, so a spent Satchel is 20 seconds of a mage who cannot leave. Keep trading at contact whenever the minefield is down; nothing in his kit out-scales you in lane.

edits.before: By first item your passive burst alone can delete Ziggs in an all-in, and he has nothing at close range to answer it. Use Heroic Swing to skip past his poke zone, then finish with Comeuppance if he tries to kite or flee. In teamfights he's a walking pick for your R the moment he's caught without his satchel up.
edits.after: By first item a full string plus swing autos deletes him, and at close range his only answers move you rather than stop you. Swing past the poke zone, then hold Comeuppance for after Satchel Charge fires — it displaces him, so a bullet released into it lands on nothing. Caught without Satchel, he is a free pick.

notes: MC_REAL_GAMES has 924 games here, so the matchup was audited. The page's core error was treating Ziggs as out-ranged and helpless at contact: Bouncing Bomb is exactly the same 850 range as Avengerang and recharges roughly twice as fast, and Akshan has no 'empowered auto' or 'melee-auto range' as the text claimed. The two cooldowns that actually decide the lane — Hexplosive Minefield at a flat 16 seconds and Satchel Charge at 20 — were absent or unnumbered. DATA NOTE: the derived flags on Ziggs' W include percentHealth ('punishes HP stacking'), and _missing/akshan_mid.json raises a 'resistances-invalidated' interaction on that basis, but Riot's own Satchel Charge description says only that it deals magic damage and knocks enemies away. I trusted the description and wrote nothing about percent-health damage or bypassed resistances; if the flag is right, that interaction is still unwritten.
